question: What host authorization model should experimental Claws use for stdio MCP commands and reuse of a globally named MCP declaration?
rationale: The patch can be mechanically adjusted only after maintainers choose whether Claw-provided commands must use a broker/allowlist and whether global exact-match sharing is permitted, namespaced, or explicitly host-authorized.

options.title: Pause for a security contract
options.body: Hold this PR until the RFC/owners define the command broker and the authorization rule for sharing a global MCP declaration.

options.title: Broker and namespace MCP resources
options.body: Require Claw declarations to resolve through a host-controlled launcher and isolate MCP resources by Claw or installation identity.

options.title: Permit explicit host-approved sharing
options.body: Keep the global namespace only when a host-owned authorization record explicitly approves each shared declaration and owner set.

recommendation.title: Pause for a security contract
recommendation.body: Hold this PR until the RFC/owners define the command broker and the authorization rule for sharing a global MCP declaration.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned to the PR and has already reviewed the lifecycle/config ownership contracts that the decision affects.
